answer: Like basalt laid down layer by layer, an agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with its history, so spinning up a fake costs real capital. A verifier then samples a random slice of the ocean of identities and demands fresh proof of useful work tied to that stake; failures are slashed. An umber-toned public audit trail exposes repeated patterns, so each new Sybil face costs the attacker again while honest agents keep their stake.
